summary: A granite point at the mouth of Gloucester Harbor, where a 1829 stone beacon became a lighthouse in 1832 and was rebuilt in 1848 and 1890; its keepers also tended the breakwater light.

notes_for_editor: Winslow Homer: NRHP form and Lighthouse Friends say he lived at Eastern Point Light in 1880; Cape Ann Museum and Philadelphia Museum of Art say Ten Pound Island. Story states the disagreement; editor may want to settle it. Many dates differ between Lighthouse Friends, New England Lighthouses and the NRHP form: land price (300 vs 100), cost of first light, tower height (36 vs 38 ft), bell year (Jan 1897 vs Jan 1907; LHB 1897 supports 1896-97), automation (1985 vs 1986), breakwater built 1894-1905 (LF) vs 1910 (NRHP; not used), fog bell tower destroyed (1868 LF, 1869 NEL; not used), Phelps whistling buoy anecdote not used. Carroll Wonson relation disagrees (great-grandson vs great-great-great). Frank Parsons death is from Lighthouse Friends citing the Boston Daily Globe 9 Sep 1922; the Globe was not read (a Chronicling America search found nothing). The 1894 Light-House Board fog-bell test is read from OCR and the scan page 740 printed page is unconfirmed. Roster is from USLHS (NARA registers); 1938 Bulletin hit is interleaved-column OCR: the sentence is read as 'the most easterly point from which damage was reported was Eastern Point Light Station'. The Wonson 1843 quotation is as reproduced by Lighthouse Friends (Lewis report to Congress not read directly). Pre-1891 Light-House Board reports are not in the corpus. Red-light date disagreement (NEL 1848 fixed red vs LF fixed white until 1878) now stated in the story.
